issues.legal_issue: A subtenant created with the landlord’s consent is entitled to have the subtenant’s comparative hardship considered in a landlord’s application to release the premises.
material_facts: The tenant inducted the appellant as a subtenant with the landlords’ consent, and that consent had been established in earlier litigation between the parties.
The appellant paid rent to the tenant, who paid rent to the landlords.
The landlords applied to obtain release of the premises for their personal use.
The authorities allowed release against the appellant without considering the appellant’s likely hardship, reasoning that the statutory protection did not extend to a subtenant.
issues.conclusion: The subtenant was entitled to the protection requiring comparative hardship to be considered. Because the authorities failed to consider the subtenant’s hardship, the decisions on that issue were set aside and the matter was remanded for consideration of the likely hardship to both the subtenant and the landlords.
issues.legal_principle: The fourth proviso to section 21 of the Uttar Pradesh Urban Buildings (Regulation of Letting, Rent and Eviction) Act, 1972 requires the prescribed authority to consider the likely hardship to the tenant from granting release against the likely hardship to the landlord from refusing release. Under sections 3(a) and 3(j), the rent relationship makes the subtenant a tenant vis-à-vis the tenant-in-chief, who is the subtenant’s landlord; where the subtenancy was created with the landlord’s consent, the subtenant’s possession is not illegal and the subtenant is not excluded from the proviso’s protection. The Court also referred to Bhullan Singh v. Babu Ram, (1965) A.L.J. 544, which treated a subtenant as included within the term “tenant” under an earlier rent-control enactment.

predicates.release_application_proceeding: A landlord sought release of rented premises through a statutory proceeding to recover possession.
predicates.subtenancy_created_with_landlord_consent: The tenant inducted another person as a subtenant with the landlord’s consent.
predicates.subtenant_pays_rent_to_head_tenant: The subtenant paid rent to the tenant-in-chief.

issues.definition: When a landlord seeks release of premises and the subtenancy was created with the landlord’s consent and the subtenant pays rent to the tenant-in-chief, the subtenant’s hardship must be considered before release.
